description: 1 Thessalonians 5:16 read aloud in Greek (a synthesized voice): whatever the scorer heard, the note never quotes the verse as written, 'Πάντοτε χαίρετε', as what was heard (his screenshot: the note quoted it while both words were marked to fix), names what was heard in plain letters, and never uses the past tense of read, which the English voice speaks as 'reed'.

request.pronunciation_guide: Modern Greek, as Greek is spoken in Greece today: never by English spelling habit and never by the Erasmian (school) pronunciation. The app respells a word in syllables, the stressed one in capitals: ταῦτα is TAF-ta, Πάντοτε is PAN-do-te, χαίρετε is HYE-re-te. αυ and ευ are af and ef before θ κ ξ π σ τ φ χ ψ, and av and ev before a voiced consonant or a vowel (never "aw", never "ow"); ηυ is eef or eev the same way. αι is e; ει, οι, υι, η, ι and υ are ee; ου is oo; ω and ο are o. β is v; δ is dh as in "this"; γ is gh (or y before e or i); θ is th as in "thin"; φ is f; χ is kh, the ch of "loch", before a, o, ou and a consonant, and the softer hy before e or i. μπ, ντ and γκ are b, d and g at the start of a word and mb, nd and ng inside it; γγ is ng; γχ is ng plus kh (or hy before e or i); γξ is nks. σ is z before β γ δ ζ λ μ ν ρ. A doubled consonant is said once. Both breathings are silent, and the iota under a letter is not said.
